notes: Account evaluating Redwood Dedicated for latency-sensitive customer support chat and high-throughput reranking for fraud detection.
Primary concern: exact definition and measurement of latency SLOs (p50/p95/p99) across streaming and non-streaming modes.
They want client-side timing aligned with server-side telemetry or a clearly documented delta. Asking: do p99 numbers come from server ingestion-to-last-token, or from client RTT including network?
Preference to have separate SLOs for streaming vs non-streaming endpoints (streaming p95/p99 measured at last-chunk-to-client, non-streaming measured end-to-end response time).

Throughput targets: baseline 2000 concurrent chat sessions, peak burst 5K qps for short windows; token throughput estimated 10M tokens/day. Need guidance on reserved GPU sizing and expected sustained throughput per GPU for their model family.

Cost sensitivity: willing to commit to reserved capacity if predictable latency guarantees + clear autoscale/burst policy. Wants cost modeling for 3 configurations (baseline, baseline+burst, high-availability multi-region).

Security/compliance: must run in VPC or on-prem for regulated PII workflows. SOC2 + SSO and KMS envelope encryption required. Audit logging retention 7 years for some workflows; asked about retention controls and export APIs.

Quote from CTO: "We can tolerate p95 ~200ms for simple chat queries, but p99 spikes above 500ms are unacceptable for downstream UX. We need concrete measurement and mitigation (fallbacks, model variants) in SLA."

AE notes: emphasized Redwood routing/fallbacks and Optimize recommendations for batching/caching. AE proposed a 2-week POC with dedicated 2xA100 equivalent pool, synthetic benchmarks + a small production shadow run.

SE notes: need to validate streaming measurement. Current Redwood documentation shows server-side p99 measured at server emit of last token; Aurora insists on client-side 95/99 which includes network. Proposal: agree on both metrics in SLA and include conversion guidance.
Legal asked for availability SLA with credits and a clear definition of downtime windows (scheduled maintenance vs unplanned). Also need data residency clause for EU customer subset.

POC plan: week 1 - baseline throughput bench (chat non-streaming), week 2 - streaming latency bench and p99 analysis, week 3 - shadow traffic for small subset of users, week 4 - finalize sizing and SLA draft.
Reference artifacts: pricing deck shared (drive link), security FAQ in drive, Fireflies transcript from 2026-01-12 contains p99 quote and CTO notes.
Open question: how will p99 be computed for streaming when partial tokens are returned across many chunks? They want definition whether last-chunk arrival or first-byte-to-last-byte is used.

requirements_summary: Latency SLOs: explicit p50/p95/p99 targets for streaming and non-streaming endpoints
Measurement alignment: provide both server-side and client-side timing definitions and a mapping/conversion approach
Streaming specifics: define p99 as time from client request to last-chunk visible to client (or alternatively provide last-chunk server emit + network RTT estimate)
Non-streaming specifics: end-to-end response latency measured at server completion; client wants end-to-end including network for contract metrics
Throughput: sustain 2000 concurrent sessions; burst to 5000 qps; token/day ~10M
Reserved GPU planning: expected A100-class pool sizing with headroom for 2x baseline for HA and burst; need per-GPU throughput estimates for targeted models
SLA expectations: uptime SLA, latency SLOs with credit formulas, scheduled maintenance windows spelled out
Security: VPC or on-prem deployment, SOC2 compliance, SSO/SAML integration, KMS support, audit log retention controls
